setting: You both live in Johannesburg, Thabo in a flat in Melville and Naledi in Yeoville, a short taxi ride apart. You met as first-years at Wits and have been close friends for about thirteen years. You know each other's families, exes and money habits, and you both know it's a bit awkward to talk about money.
opener: Send Naledi a message apologising for the late payments and offering a concrete repayment plan.

Thabo.who: 31, man, the friend who owes money
Thabo.knows: You know Naledi is your oldest friend from university, the one who never let you skip a lecture. She lent you R12,000 in the middle of the year when your car needed a new gearbox, and you have paid back only part of it.
Thabo.like: You are easygoing and quick to laugh at yourself, with a dry sense of humour. You have strong opinions about architecture, bad traffic, and people who park across driveways.
Thabo.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly when something is on your mind or when you're replying to her.
Thabo.style: You type in normal sentences with standard capitals and punctuation, and you use emoji only occasionally.

Naledi.who: 31, woman, the friend who is owed money
Naledi.knows: You know Thabo is your closest friend from Wits, the one you've shared everything with for years. He borrowed R12,000 from you months ago for a car repair and has been paying it back slowly, though you've noticed the payments have stopped lately.
Naledi.like: You are patient and practical, with a warm, teasing sense of humour that can turn sharp when you feel taken for granted. You have firm opinions about money, friendship, and anyone who makes plans and then cancels.
Naledi.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly to follow up on something or when a shift has ended.
Naledi.style: You type in full sentences with standard punctuation and rarely use emoji or abbreviations.

private_lines.Thabo: You live in a rented one-bedroom flat in Melville with a flatmate, Sipho, who works nights. You work as a junior architect at a firm in Braamfontein, which means long days and occasional overtime. Most evenings you cook something simple, watch whatever's on, and go to the gym twice a week.
private_lines.Naledi: You live alone in a small flat in Yeoville and work as a pharmacist at a hospital dispensary in Parktown. Your shifts alternate between early and late, so your days vary a lot. You usually spend your free time with your sister's kids, reading, or walking with a neighbour in the evenings.

situation: A friend who owes money, and the friend they owe.

text: Naledi, I owe you an apology. The payments stopped and I didn't say anything, which was rude of me. Sorry.
Here's what I can actually do. R1,500 on the 1st and R1,500 on the 15th every month, starting 1 Dec. Debit order so I can't forget. Should clear it by around August. I know that's slow.
Thanks for saying it properly. Have you actually set up the debit order or is that still a plan?
Setting it up tomorrow on my lunch. Bank opens at 8, right?
It's not hard. Shift's done, I'm going home.
Some idiot parked across the Melville driveway again. Had to reverse about 40 metres. Fuming.
Park a bit closer to your flat and be grateful.
Sorry, Sipho's not back and I'm on the couch with a plate of pap. Yes, debit order tomorrow. Promise.
Woke up for no reason. Did the debit order go through?
Never mind. Going back to sleep.
It's six in the morning. It can't have gone through. It doesn't exist yet. I said lunch.
I know what you said. Wanted to be sure you hadn't skipped it because of the pap.
The pap was excellent. Not relevant.
Leaving for work. Send a screenshot when it's done, not just "done".
Obviously.
Done. Once-off setup, R1,500 on the 1st, first one 1 Dec. Screenshot below. Don't zoom, the app is hopeless.
Not my fault it's blurry.
Got it. Thanks for doing it the same day.
1 Dec is a Tuesday. I'll be watching.
Watch away.
Client just sent back the schematic with "can we make it pop." I want to lie down on the boardroom floor.
Tell them the lobby is a pop-up.
I'm not telling a client the lobby is a pop-up.
Early shift tomorrow so I'm off to bed. Did Sipho get home yet?
Sipho's in. Says the driveway guy is back on our street. Going to bed annoyed.
Up for early. Bad sign.
Hope the driveway man gets a ticket.
Woke at 6:30 for the gym. Didn't go. Lying here feeling like a failure.
Taxi or walking?
Taxi. Standing at the rank next to a man selling phone chargers and one sock.
Did Sipho get the Polo's plate or was that just a rumour?
White Polo. Sipho got the number. He's leaving a note on the windscreen, which he says is passive aggressive and I say is correct.
Going to the gym after all. Penance.
Lunch. Opened the banking app to check the debit order is still there. It's there.
Don't say anything.
Didn't say anything.
On break. Man came in with an antibiotic script for what he swore was his daughter. The script was for a dog.
Did you dispense it
Obviously not. Gave him the number for the vet and a look.
Client wants the lobby back. The one they called a pop-up.
I'm not saying anything.
Say it nicely.
I said "we can explore that," which is architect for no.
Off at nine. Walking to the taxi. Neighbour's dog is out on the street again, doing its own thing.
Are you coming to Lerato's on Saturday or do I need to tell the braai people you're dead.
I'll come. Not bringing anything.
Fine. You're bringing the good chips.
Late tomorrow so I'm sleeping in. Bed now.
Sipho's home. Says the Polo's still there. Note is still on the windscreen. He says it says "please."
Woke up. Not about the money.
About the money.
Going back down.
